source.title: Neural computations underlying arbitration between model-based and model-free learning.

confidence_rationale: Direct human fMRI evidence that a dedicated neural arbitrator encodes each controller's RELIABILITY and the comparison between reliabilities, and that it acts by DOWN-MODULATING the losing controller's valuation pathway. That last finding is the strongest single piece of external support for ARC-120's specific shape -- authority is actively withheld from an existing computation, not merely unclaimed. Held below 0.85 by fMRI's indirectness and by the same momentary-vs-developmental gap that limits Daw 2005.
failure_signatures: An architecture in which the gate is implemented only at the winner's side (the competent module simply writes/acts) and never suppresses the incompetent module's ongoing influence leaves the losing controller's valuation signal intact -- the opposite of the negative modulation Lee et al. observe.

If a system carries no explicit representation of per-module reliability, there is nothing for an arbitrator to compare, and any resulting gate is necessarily a fixed architectural prior rather than an earned-authority mechanism.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Inferior lateral prefrontal and frontopolar cortex encode the reliability of model-based and model-free predictions and the output of a comparison between them; connectivity from these regions to model-free valuation areas is negatively modulated by the degree of model-based control, suggesting arbitration works by suppressing the model-free valuation system when the arbitrator deems the model-based system should drive behaviour.
mapping.ree_translation: Behavioural authority is allocated by an explicit, separately-represented competence signal (prediction reliability) and is enforced by actively SUPPRESSING the non-selected computation's influence on valuation -- not by leaving it to win or lose on its own merits. For ARC-120 this is the mechanistic form the 'competence -> authority' step takes in a brain: a dedicated arbitrator, an explicit reliability variable per module, and a gate that acts on the loser rather than only enabling the winner.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human fMRI in a two-stage Markov decision task; reliability here is a trial-by-trial estimate of prediction error variance in a value-learning system, and the authority at stake is action selection only. It does not test write/consolidation authority, does not test a developmental ordering, and cannot speak to whether REE's four existing gates share a single principle. BOLD connectivity modulation is correlational and does not establish that the frontopolar signal causes the suppression.
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI, healthy adults, two-stage sequential-decision (Markov) task with varying state-transition uncertainty and reward stochasticity.

confidence_components.notes: Strong venue and design; the reliability-comparison regressor and the negative-modulation finding are exactly the two things ARC-120 needs, which lifts mapping_fidelity above the Daw 2005 entry despite fMRI's weaker source quality relative to a canonical theory paper. Transfer risk stays moderate: human decision-making to a computational substrate, and correlational connectivity evidence.
